paragraphs.text: The Star Trek series is characterized by its diversity of characters and species . To reflect this, no cards will be typed as Alien in the upcoming Universes Beyond Star Trek set. Instead, all the different species will have their own creature type instead. The following Star Trek specific aliens are expected to appear as crossover species in Magic: The Gathering .

Andorian ( 1 card , 3 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a blue-skinned humanoid alien species featuring a pair of antennae on top of their heads. Andorians are a militaristic race and known for their determination and endurance in physical combat. The race is a founding member of the United Federation of Planets .
The Aenar subspecies has white skin and, unlike mainstream Andorians, are blind and telepathic.
Borg ( 7 cards , 9 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a pseudo-species of cybernetic humanoids, or cyborgs , from the Delta Quadrant .

Individual Borg are known as drones . Together they form the Borg Collective. Their ultimate goal is the attainment of 'perfection' through the forcible assimilation of diverse sentient species, technologies, and knowledge which is added and absorbed into the hive mind . As a result, the Borg are among the most powerful and feared entities in the galaxy, without really being a true species at all.
The Borg are artifact creatures that have the same ability as (one-sided) slivers . Each card grants their ability to all other artifact creatures controlled by its player.
The assimilate ability is exclusive to the Borg.

Borgs are explicitely excluded from the Federation ability word, to reflect how the Borgs aren't part of the Federation and to avoid any interaction with the Changeling mechanic. It is similar to the "non- Brushwagg " clause used in Unfinity on Embiggen .

Caitian ( 1 card , 3 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a humanoid alien species with feline features, such as short faces, triangular ears, large eyes with vertically slitted pupils, whiskers, fangs, and a tail. They have sharp claws on their hands and feet, and most are entirely covered with fur. When they need to move quickly, Caitians can switch to quadrupedal locomotion, displaying feline agility and reaction times. They also possess an extremely high pain tolerance, far more than most other humanoid species.
Gorn ( 2 cards , 3 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a bipedal reptilian species from the Beta Quadrant .

The Gorn are a cold-blooded species, with green, rubbery skin, red blood, and an average height of approximately two meters. They tend to be many times stronger than most humanoids. While young Gorn are very agile and fast, adults tend to be slower and less agile but with greater stamina. Gorn hatch from parasitic eggs that incubate inside humanoid hosts. When maturated, the hatchlings or younglings rip their way violently from the body of their host. Newly emerged Gorn are white in color; they become green as they feed voraciously and grew rapidly in size, molting their skin in the process. The hatchlings are quadrupedal and exceptionally fast and strong, and posses prehensile tails. They are uncontrollably aggressive toward other lifeforms and even members of their own species.

Kelpien ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent tall humanoid aliens with a lanky build, brownish orange skin, and no head hair. Tendril-like threat ganglia splay out from the back of a Kelpien's head when they sense danger.

The species map on the Kelpien's homeplanet was a binary of predator or prey. Kelpiens are the latter, and as such are biologically determined with heightened senses, and a hyper-vigilance to detect approaching danger in order to flee from it. This had been honed to the point of essentially a sixth-sense warning that a situation is dangerous. After undergoing a certain maturing proces the Kelpien's excessive fear responses are suppressed, and they develop more aggressive physiques.
Klingon ( 10 cards , 21 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent an aggressive humanoid warrior race of aliens with a sagittal crest .

Klingons are characterized by prideful ruthlessness and brutality, bolstered by a strict warrior code. One of the major powers of the galaxy, the Klingons are a proud, tradition-bound people who value honor and combat. The combative Klingon culture has made them an interstellar military power to be respected and feared.

Klingon head shapes differ between houses and individuals, with some having skulls that extend backwards into an elongated cone shape. The characteristic ridges begin on the forehead and often continue over the skull. In some cases they are missing.

Lanthanite ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a humanoid species that is almost indistinguishable from humans. They posses an extremely long life span, described as "almost forever".
Orion ( 1 card , 2 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a humanoids race of aliens with a distinctive green skin. They usually have green or black hair.

Orion society is matriarchal. Orion females may be physically abusive to assert dominance over males, even if that male is a blood relative. Some female Orions are capable of emitting highly potent pheromones that can impact the physiology of other species. Female members of the Orion Syndicate sometimes posed as enslaved persons in order to use their pheromones to manipulate or even control hapless would-be male slavers from other species.
Q ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a species of nigh-omnipotent and immortal non-corporeal entities that can appear in any form they wish.

All male and female individuals of the species refer to each other as "Q". It is also the name of their race. The Q live in the " Q Continuum " – an alternate dimension accessible to only the Q and their "invited" guests. The true nature of the realm is said to be beyond the comprehension of "lesser beings" such as humans , therefore it is shown to humans only in ways they can understand; e.g., a run-down gas station in the "middle of nowhere".

The Q are fascinated with humans. Humans are constantly growing and changing. The Q are all-powerful beings who have stopped growing a long time ago. This makes them very bored. Experimenting with humans provides the Q a distraction, and possibly a means to regain a future for the Q race.

Romulan ( 0 cards , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a militaristic humanoid race of aliens with pointed ears, arched and up-swept eyebrows and green blood. Some Romulans have two brow ridges above the bridge of their nose, forming a V-shape on the forehead, while other Romulans lack these ridges, making them outwardly indistinguishable from Vulcans . The race values fierce loyalty, extreme secrecy, and unchecked ambition.

The Romulans are biological cousins of the Vulcans, descended from those who rejected Surak 's reforms during the "Time of Awakening". By the 24th century, the Romulan Star Empire was one of the major powers in the galaxy.
Talosian ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a telepathic humanoid alien species. They are small, slim, pale creatures with large elongated heads.

Talosians were once a warp-capable, technologically advanced culture but a nuclear holocaust left their planet virtually uninhabitable and killed most of the species. The survivors of the nuclear war congregated in underground dwellings, where they became dependent upon their own mental powers, which they used to create stunningly real illusions. They are known to experiment with humans to gain an understanding of their nature.
Tellarite ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a warp-capable pig -like humanoid species. Their homeworld became a founding member of the United Federation of Planets .

Tellarites are a stout species with an average body height shorter than that of Humans. They have distinctive snouts, often have beards, and their hands are sometimes hoof-like in appearance. Their lower jaw usually possesses a pair of tusks. Tellarites are known to be an impatient people. They are also known for their "stubborn pride" and have a propensity toward strong emotion. Tellarites enjoy a good argument. They often begin an interaction with a series of complaints or insults. Because of their ability to argue, and hence their skills in debate, Tellarites make excellent politicians.
Tholian ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a crystalline-based non-humanoid alien species.

Tholians have a hard carapace that is chiefly mineral, featuring six thin legs that makes it possible to move in any direction quickly. The legs are attached at the base of the torso and are radially symmetric. They also have two arms that end in multi-fingered hands. They have a slightly visible neck that is covered by a semitransparent dome membrane that shields the head. Two glowing spots near the top of their torso may be some sort of information-gathering organ. Tholian biology requires high temperatures. They can tolerate lower temperatures for a brief period of time, but their carapace can fracture if exposed for a longer time. They communicate through a series of clicks and chirps.
Tosk ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a humanoid race of aliens with reptilian skin, native to the Gamma Quadrant .

Tosk, meaning "The Hunted", do not have personal designations, and "Tosk" essentially sums up everything about them and their purpose in life. They are bred and trained to become the quarry in a ritual hunt for another species, known as the Hunters, who track them, capture them, return them to their homeworld, and ritualistically kill them. Tosk are only sentient because the Hunters made them that way. Tosk can make themselves invisible to the naked eye. They also have great agility and only require seventeen minutes of rest per rotation.
Vorta ( 1 card , 1 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a humanoid species that is genetically-engineered by the Founders of the Dominion .

Vorta have pale skin, violet eyes, and elongated ears that are completely joined to the rest of the head. The Founders altered the Vorta genome to include a sense of hearing greater than that of most other humanoid races, but they have comparatively weak eyesight. Vorta are immune to most forms of poison. They acts as field commanders, administrators, scientists, and diplomats for the Dominion. If a Vorta is killed, they may be with a clone , which retains all the memories of their predecessor through an unspecified process.
Vulcan ( 5 cards , 12 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a stoic humanoid race of aliens with pointed ears and complete control over their emotions.

Like their Romulan cousins, Vulcans are characterized by their ears, arched eyebrows, and green blood. The Vulcan mindset is defined by strict logic, reason, and emotional control. Vulcans actually feel emotions much more strongly than humans. To survive, they actively suppress these feelings using deep mental training to avoid chaos. Their core philosophy was founded by an ancient teacher named Surak .
Xindi ( 1 card , 2 artworks ) is a creature type used to represent a group of six alien species who have all developed on the same planet.

The Xindi-Avians are believed extinct, as the result of a brutal civil war between the six species that destroyed the planet. Each of the five remaining species have their own distinct opinion about which is the dominant species, all separately favoring their own. The Primates, Arboreals, and Reptilians speak a common language. The Insectoids and Aquatics understand this language, but appear to be physically incapable of speaking it.
